narrative:
The model estimated a 53.1% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is only slightly above a coin flip, but because it crossed the 50% threshold used for the admission decision, your law school application was rejected.

The strongest reason was your third-year class-rank position: you were in the second decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. This was the most influential factor and it pushed the prediction toward bar exam failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.30 was slightly above the accepted-student average of 3.23, and it was the second most important factor; this worked in your favor and pushed toward passing. Your law school admission test score of 35 was below the accepted-student average of about 37.2, and it was the third most important factor; it pushed the prediction back toward failure.

To improve your chances, ask admissions what would strengthen a future application, focus on raising your admission test score, and seek academic support or additional coursework that demonstrates readiness for rigorous law study. You may also consider delaying reapplication until you can show stronger third-year academic performance or a higher test score.
